superedges.prose: The paper treats detecting distributional shift and responding to it as two separate problems, and splits the response tools out into formal-methods-imported. Covariate shift, partially specified models, unsupervised risk estimation, and training on multiple distributions are all ways of detecting or bounding confidence around a shift once it may have occurred. Reachability analysis and robust policy improvement, both formal-methods-imported members, are introduced immediately afterward as candidate responses, falling back to a conservative baseline policy once out-of-distribution operation is suspected. The paper flags the seam explicitly: to its authors' knowledge, this control-theoretic work has "not yet been combined with methods for detecting out-of-distribution failures of a model" (concrete-problems, §"How to respond when out-of-distribution.", p. 18). Neither theme's own narrative registers this as unfinished; each describes its half of the pipeline, detection or response, as though it were the whole story.

The two reframings are not fully independent. The paper's own transition between them names partially specified models, a statistical-relaxations technique, as the first of several routes to the weaker, checkable contracts that machine learning with contracts calls for: partially specified models "offer one approach to this," while "reachability analysis and model repair provide other avenues for obtaining better contracts" (concrete-problems, §"A unifying view: counterfactual reasoning and machine learning with contracts.", p. 19). Covariate shift, the generalized method of moments, and unsupervised risk estimation stay inside classical statistics, treating shift as a matter of which assumption to relax; partially specified models already produces the kind of partial, explicit specification a contract needs. What the contracts framing supplies is not a new technique but an obligation: state that specification openly and check it, rather than silently assume it holds.

Formal-methods-imported's link to distributional shift splits along a fault line neither theme names on its own. Reachability analysis and robust policy improvement appear earlier, in the same section, as reactive fallbacks, conservative baseline policies to switch to once shift is suspected, independent of any contract language. Model repair is different: the paper introduces it only inside the contracts discussion, as the technique for restoring a violated contract after the fact by altering an already-trained model, rather than switching to a pre-built conservative policy (concrete-problems, §"A unifying view: counterfactual reasoning and machine learning with contracts.", p. 19). Formal-methods-imported therefore reaches shift-as-contracts-and-causation through exactly one of its six members, and that member does a structurally different job, post-hoc repair of the model itself, than the two control-theoretic tools the same toolkit lends to statistical-relaxations-for-distributional-shift's detection problem instead.

Both exclusions surface in the paper's Section 8 survey of related efforts, but they exclude different kinds of things. The Futurist Community entry, source of long-term-ai-risk-framing, distances accidents from a rival framing of the same underlying concern: MIRI is credited with having studied several of this paper's own concepts, "wireheading, environmental embedding, counterfactual reasoning," "albeit at a more philosophical level," before the paper positions its empirical, near-term focus as complementary rather than opposed (concrete-problems, §"Futurist Community:", p. 20). The Related Problems in Safety entry, source of adjacent-research-areas' six fields, excludes not a rival framing but rival subject matter: privacy, fairness, security, abuse, transparency, and policy name different harms entirely, discrimination, adversarial attack, data exposure, that a system could commit while causing no accident at all. The paper's self-scoping thus runs along two independent axes: how to talk about accident risk, and what counts as accident risk in the first place.

Asimov's first law is the one concept framing-accidents-vs-speculative-risk and formal-methods-imported both claim, and the paper faults it on two independent axes depending on which register picks it up. As a way of talking about safety, it fails for being monolithic: "robots must not harm humans" offers no decomposition, where accidents-in-ml immediately fractures harm into five separately tractable technical causes. As a candidate route to a machine-checkable safety property, it fails for being informal: Weld and Etzioni's 1994 attempt to formalize it within classical planning is set against the complete formal verification of the federal aircraft collision-avoidance system, real engineering rigor achieved for cyber-physical systems that the same section admits has "not focused much on modern machine learning systems" (concrete-problems, §"Cyber-Physical Systems Community:", p. 20). One fictional sentence anchors both of the paper's self-boundary exercises, undercut on granularity in one and on rigor in the other.
